system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: The system prompt for the first part of the agent execution simply states “Execute the following plan:...”followed by the plan provided by the Planner.
system_prompt_style.note: Per-agent system prompts with task/plan variables rendered in.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: a generalized execution flow applicable to any application defined by a user prompt
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/environment context injection; tasks are web/finance/paper tasks driven by MCP tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: the execution agent is asked to summarizeonly the relevant informationfrom the stage to be passed to future stages

observation_format.evidence_quote: Fetch tool takes the URL of a website and the offset character length as an input and returns clean text content for that web page.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: a set of available functions, defined as JSON schema objects within the tools parameter

tool_count.note: Tool count varies by application and MCP servers exposed; no fixed default set.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: theFile Systemserver enables seamless read/write operations with the local file system
edit_primitive.note: Only write-file tool described; no structured edit primitive.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: The Stage agent also has the list of MCP tools descriptions from the MCP server or even the Doc String of a Python function as possible actions.
tool_schema_source.note: Structured outputs schemas are auto-created from pydantic classes; tool schemas come from MCP servers.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: We also leverage Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and propose two alternative approaches for deploying MCP servers as cloud Functions as a Service (FaaS).

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: the stage agent breaks down the task into a set of high level objectives called stages; the planner and the execution agents then processes each stage sequentially
loop_primitives.note: Executor loops tool call + reflection within a stage.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: AgentX employs a two-tier hierarchy where theStage Generation Agentfirst creates a high-level, coarse grained plan (stages), and then thePlanner Agent creates a detailed, fine grained plan for each stage.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: AgentX enforces specialized, functional roles (Stage Generation,Planner,Executor)
multi_agent_topology.note: Fixed hand-off sequence Stage -> Planner -> Executor per stage.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: Each stage is then passed to the Planner Agent for execution.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: Given a user task, the stage agent breaks down the task into a set of high level objectives called stages
human_in_loop.note: No approval or gating step described anywhere in the execution sequence.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: These results are later saved in a local variable which is used to provide context to the first phase of the execution agent.
short_term_state.note: Stages list, plans and execution-result summaries maintained as structured outputs.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: In its current form, AgentX lacks a dedicated recovery system.
long_term_memory.note: No cross-run memory described; stage summaries are within-run only.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: AgentX executes applications by breaking them down into stages. These stages as of now are executed in a linear fashion one after the other.

self_verification.evidence_quote: first ensures that this agentunderstandsthe plan andcallsthe tools, and subsequentlyreflectson the output of the tools
self_verification.note: Evaluation-time LLM scoring is for the study, not the harness loop.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Such runs leads to failures since there lacks a dedicated recovery system in AgentX.
retry_policy.note: Executor may retry within a stage (code syntax errors), but no task-level retry.

rollback.evidence_quote: Without proper guardrails and retry mechanisms, agents can fail, provide incorrect information, or produce improper outputs.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: the execution agent is passed two attributes in its output schema: theexecution resultsand aflagto denote if the plan has successfully executed or not
termination_condition.note: Run ends when all stages complete; no step or cost cap described. AgentX 'could potentially get stuck in a loop'.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: AgentX focuses explicitly on memory consolidation.
cost_controls.note: Context summarization reduces cost but no explicit budget, routing or caching mechanism is described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: It is prone to the non deterministic nature of agentic workflow where it could potentially get stuck in a loop.
timeouts.note: No harness timeout described; Lambda-side limits not stated.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: All patterns and their agents execute on a Dell Precision 3440 with Intel Core i5-10500 processor (6 cores, 12 threads) and 16 GB RAM, running Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS
execution_isolation.note: Default local MCP servers run on the same workstation; FaaS variant deploys containerized MCP servers on AWS Lambda.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: theFile Systemserver enables seamless read/write operations with the local file system

network_policy.evidence_quote: theSerperserver enables web searches using the Google Serper API

permission_model.evidence_quote: When tools are specified to be executed by the Agent, our AgentX framework invokes the tool
permission_model.note: Planner tool-filtering limits which tools are exposed, but no authorization check before execution.

tracing.evidence_quote: It does not depend on external frameworks. The execution trace is returned by each module.

replayability.evidence_quote: To ensure consistency and reproducible outputs, the temperature and top_p were set to their default value of 1.0.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: We implement our AgentX pattern using a Python framework consisting of modules for the different agent types and an orchestrator between the agents to implement the interaction pattern.
eval_hooks.note: Accuracy scoring was done externally with an OpenAI 4o-mini judge for the study, not shipped as a harness hook.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Without proper guardrails and retry mechanisms, agents can fail, provide incorrect information, or produce improper outputs.

target_domain.evidence_quote: Agentic systems often struggle when faced with numerous tools, complex multi-step tasks, and long-context management to track history and avoid hallucinations.
target_domain.note: Generic agentic workflow pattern over FaaS-hosted MCP tools; evaluated on three applications not named in excerpts.

open_source.note: No repository URL or licence stated in the paper.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: For all our experiments, we utilized OpenAI’s gpt-4o-mini large language model, accessed via their public cloud API.
model_agnostic.note: Uses the official openai Python library directly; no provider abstraction described.
